sets.title: D. Sentence structure and usage
sets.intro: Choose the option that correctly completes each sentence. 47 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: ____ not a single hard-surfaced road during the entire colonial period aside from city streets.
questions.e: Existential there + singular noun (road): There was.

questions.q: ____ in 1776 that the Declaration of Independence was signed.
questions.e: Cleft sentence for emphasis: It was in 1776 that ...

questions.q: ____ more than 300,000 people in Philadelphia by the end of the colonial period, making it the largest city in the colonies.
questions.e: Existential there + plural noun (people): There were.

questions.q: In the eighteenth century, ____ not many women who had access to formal education in the colonies.
questions.e: Existential there with plural women: there were not many women.

questions.q: After the Revolution, although some advances were made in education, ____ a slow process.
questions.e: It was a slow process: it refers to education's progress.

questions.q: The behavior of many volcanoes ____ very difficult to predict, especially the more explosive types.
questions.e: The subject is behavior (singular), not volcanoes: is.

questions.q: ____ more than 2000 minerals are known, nearly all rocks are formed from seven mineral groups.
questions.e: Although introduces a concession clause: Although more than 2000 minerals are known, ...

questions.q: Alexander Graham Bell worked with deaf students before ____ the first telephone in 1876.
questions.e: After the preposition before, use -ing: before designing.

questions.q: An enzyme works by coming in contact with a particular substance ____ with it, and changing it.
questions.e: Parallel -ing forms: coming ..., combining ..., and changing.

questions.q: Foods of animal origin generally supply greater amounts of iron to the diet than ____
questions.e: After than, a comparison clause can use do + subject: than do foods of plant origin.

questions.q: ____ energy for growth or repair, a plant must carry out photosynthesis.
questions.e: Infinitive of purpose: To obtain energy, a plant must ...

questions.q: Nicotine, ____ found in tobacco, is named after the French diplomat Jean Nicot.
questions.e: An appositive (a chemical compound) renames Nicotine; no extra verb is needed.

questions.q: ____ the world’s most successful artificial language.
questions.e: A complete sentence needs a subject and verb: Esperanto is the world's most successful ...

questions.q: ____ food we eat lacks minerals, then the body can use the stores from its bones for more urgent needs.
questions.e: The if-clause pairs with then in the main clause: If the food we eat lacks minerals, then ...

questions.q: ____ an organism to become a fossil.
questions.e: The pattern is It is rare for + noun + to-infinitive.

questions.q: Among sea horses, ____ carries and hatches the eggs in a special breeding pouch.
questions.e: Cleft structure: it is the male which carries ... The other options leave no main verb or a fragment.

questions.q: ____ will be increasingly used as a source of petrochemicals when oil begins to run out.
questions.e: No doubt is a sentence adverb: No doubt coal will be increasingly used ...

questions.q: Scientists have discovered that the jelly like material in cells ____ proteins and other substances.
o: it is actually a complex mixture
actually is a complex mixture of
that actually are a complex mixture of
questions.e: The clause needs a verb and complement: actually is a complex mixture of ...

questions.q: The discovery that electricity could produce magnetism ____ in 1820 by the Danish physicist, Hans Christian Oersted.
questions.e: Passive verb phrase with agent: was made by accident in 1820 by ...

questions.q: Digital systems work first by changing quantity and then ____ into strips of numbers.
questions.e: Parallel -ing after by: changing ... and then converting ...

questions.q: It is gravity ____ the objects toward earth.
questions.e: Cleft sentence: It is gravity that pulls the objects toward earth.

questions.q: ____ their territories but rather than fight, they howl.
questions.e: The clause needs subject + verb: Wolves jealously protect their territories (adverb jealously).

questions.q: The strongest dump trucks work in rock quarries, ____ tons of rocks and soil at one time.
questions.e: Where refers to the place (rock quarries): where they move tons of rocks.

questions.q: Helen Keller lost both her sight and hearing ____ after severe illness.
questions.e: A time clause with a complete verb: when she was 19 months old.

questions.q: It is only recently that the ballets have been based on themes ____ American life.
questions.e: Reduced relative clause: themes reflecting American life.

questions.q: Built at the beginning of the century, the Library of Congress houses one of the largest ____ collections of books in the world.
questions.e: Coordinated adjectives: one of the largest and finest collections.

questions.q: In the preparation of fibrous material for production uses, stiff woody fibers from plants ____ fibers from animal sources.
questions.e: Verb + comparison: need more heat than fibers from animal sources.

questions.q: The cosmopolitan flavour of San Francisco is enhanced by ____ shops and museums.
questions.e: A possessive plus adjective before the plural noun: its many ethnic shops.

questions.q: ____ that increasing numbers of compact-disk players will be bought by consumers in the years to come.
questions.e: Passive with dummy it: It's anticipated that ...

questions.q: ____ , human beings have relatively constant body temperature.
questions.e: Like (preposition) + noun phrase: Like all animals, human beings ...

questions.q: The Louisiana Territory, an area ____ the size of France, was purchased in 1803.
questions.e: Multiplier comparison: more than 4 times the size of France.

questions.q: Despite claims that filters and low-tar tobacco make smoking somewhat safer, in fact they only marginally reduce, ____ eliminate, the hazards.
questions.e: Contrast with not: reduce, not eliminate, the hazards.

questions.q: ____ many of the designs for the new capital were considered lost forever, Benjamin Banneker helped reproduce the original plans.
questions.e: When introduces a time clause: When many of the designs were considered lost, ...

questions.q: A few natural elements exist in ____ that they are rarely seen in their natural environment.
questions.e: Such + adjective + plural noun + that: such small quantities that ...

questions.q: ____ business, a merger is a combination of two or more corporations under one management.
questions.e: The fixed phrase is In business.

questions.q: Jan’s invention, the “shoe-lasting” machine, ____ production but it cut the cost of it by half.
questions.e: Correlative pair: not only increased production but ...

questions.q: In the U.S. ____ is the most concentrated is New Orleans.
o: where the French influences the city
questions.e: A noun phrase with a relative clause: the city where French influence is the most concentrated.

questions.q: Sometimes ____ wears people out and is worse than the lack of sleep itself.
questions.e: The subject of wears is a noun phrase: the desire to sleep.

questions.q: In order to grow vegetables properly, gardeners must know ____ .
o: that the requirements for each vegetable are
what the requirements for each vegetable are
that is required by each vegetable
questions.e: A noun clause after know uses what plus normal word order: what the requirements for each vegetable are.

questions.q: Sweet and rich in nutritious value, ____ .
o: Khmer cooking uses palm sugar widely
there is a wide use of palm sugar in Khmer cooking
palm sugar is used widely in Khmer cooking
Khmer people use palm sugar widely in their cooking
questions.e: The subject must be what is sweet and rich: palm sugar. Other options leave a dangling modifier.

questions.q: ____ she recovers from amnesia, she will be able to recognize us.
questions.e: When she recovers is a time clause that fits the future result.

questions.q: The survivor knew it was ____ who had rescued him.
questions.e: After it was, formal English uses the subject form: it was she who.

questions.q: With ____ did the soldier fight relentlessly?
questions.e: After a preposition, a person takes whom: With whom did ...

questions.q: Neither Socheata nor I ____ afraid to scale Mount Everest.
questions.e: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (I): am.

questions.q: The sick baby, as well as his mother, ____ pulled through the ordeal.
questions.e: As well as does not change the subject; baby is singular, so: was.

questions.q: Please wait for me ____ that green lamp-post.
questions.e: By means beside or near: wait by that lamp-post.

questions.q: It was when he was put ____ bars that he finally turned ____ a new leaf.
questions.e: Idioms: behind bars and turn over a new leaf.

sets.title: E. Find the incorrect part
sets.intro: Each sentence has four underlined parts, marked A to D. Choose the part that contains the grammatical error. 20 questions from the NIE exam bank (corrected version). The bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: The antique collector {A|must be able} to distinguish {B|real} antiques from {C|later imitation}, which can be either reproductions {D|nor fakes}.
questions.e: Either goes with or, not nor: either reproductions or fakes.

questions.q: Paint {A|must be stirred} and {B|sometimes} {C|dilution} before it {D|is applied}.
questions.e: The second verb must be passive and parallel to must be stirred: sometimes diluted, not dilution.

questions.q: A {A|great aviation pioneer}, Amelia Earhart {B|was already famous} when she {C|sets out} on her ill-fated attempt {D|to circle} the globe in 1937.
questions.e: The story is in the past, so use the past tense: when she set out.

questions.q: Although apples {A|do not grow} during the cold season, {B|apple trees} must have {C|a such season} {D|in order to flourish}.
questions.e: Such comes before a: such a season, not a such season.

questions.q: {A|Two unique features} of the arctic {B|they are} {C|lack of precipitation} and {D|permanently frozen ground}.
questions.e: The pronoun they repeats the subject. The sentence should read: Two unique features of the arctic are ...

questions.q: {A|Faced with petroleum shortages} in the 1970s, scientists and engineers {B|in the United States} {C|stepped up its efforts} to develop more efficient heating systems and {D|better insulation}.
questions.e: The subject scientists and engineers is plural, so the pronoun is their, not its.

questions.q: Rabbits have {A|large front} {B|tooth}, short tails, and {C|hind legs and feet} adapted for {D|running and jumping}.
questions.e: The noun must be plural to match short tails: front teeth.

questions.q: Dentistry is {A|a branch of medicine} that {B|has developed} {C|very dramatic} {D|in the last twenty years}.
questions.e: An adverb is needed to modify the verb has developed: very dramatically.

questions.q: {A|The ease of solving} a jigsaw puzzle {B|depends} the number of pieces, {C|their shapes and shadings}, and {D|the design of the picture}.
questions.e: Depends needs the preposition on: depends on the number of pieces.

questions.q: Plants {A|range in size} {B|to tiny}, single-celled, {C|blue-green algae}, invisible to the naked eye, {D|to giant sequoias}, the largest living plants.
questions.e: The pattern is range from ... to ...: range in size from tiny algae to giant sequoias.

questions.q: {A|During the 1940s} science and engineering had an impact on the way {B|music reach} {C|its audience} and even influenced the way {D|in which it was composed}.
questions.e: The verb must be past and agree with the singular subject music: reached.

questions.q: By 1860 the railroads of the United States had {A|30,000 miles of track}, {B|three-quarters of which} {C|it was east} of the Mississippi River and {D|north of the Ohio River}.
questions.e: The relative clause three-quarters of which already has its subject, so it is not needed. The plural subject needs were: three-quarters of which were east of the Mississippi.

questions.q: Ballads {A|were early types} of poetry and {B|may have been} {C|among a first kinds} {D|of music}.
questions.e: Use the with first, and a cannot go with plural kinds: among the first kinds of music.

questions.q: {A|The thin outer layer} of the skin {B|is called the epidermis}, while {C|the layer inner}, {D|which is slightly thicker}, is called the dermis.
questions.e: Adjectives come before the noun: the inner layer.

questions.q: With the {A|incorporation of jazz history} into {B|current academic curricula}, {C|leading jazz musicians} {D|are now founding} on the faculties of several universities.
questions.e: The passive meaning is needed: are now found on the faculties (not founding).

questions.q: Humus, {A|a substance found in soil}, {B|is soft and spongy and enables} {C|plant roots to send out tiny hairs} {D|through that} they absorb water and food.
o: is soft and spongy and enables
plant roots to send out tiny hairs
questions.e: After a preposition, a relative pronoun for things must be which: through which they absorb water.

questions.q: Although flies {A|live longest} in cool temperatures, {B|it breed} prolifically {C|when temperatures are warm}, food is abundant, and {D|humidity is moderate}.
questions.e: The pronoun must match the plural noun flies, and the verb must agree: they breed.

questions.q: {A|Alaska's vast areas} {B|of untamed wilderness} {C|attracts} many people {D|who enjoy the outdoors}.
questions.e: The subject is the plural areas, so the verb is attract.

questions.q: The giant panda {A|closely resembles} {B|the bear}, {C|but account of} certain anatomical features {D|it is placed} in the raccoon family.
questions.e: The phrase is on account of: but on account of certain anatomical features.

questions.q: The ode {A|was original} {B|a ceremonial poem} written {C|to celebrate public occasions} {D|or exalted subjects}.
questions.e: An adverb is needed to modify the participle: was originally a ceremonial poem.

sets.title: A. Vocabulary in context
sets.intro: Choose the best word to complete each sentence. In the bank, question 1 had its answer word printed in the sentence, so it is shown here with a blank. 10 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: The ____ rain caused the river to overflow its bank.
questions.e: Incessant means never stopping: the incessant rain.

questions.q: With its ____ engine, the car performed better than we had hoped.
questions.e: A modified engine is one that has been changed and improved.

questions.q: A heavy object will ____ other objects toward it by its gravity.
questions.e: Draw means pull toward: a heavy object draws other objects toward it.

questions.q: Over the sounds of the storm, she couldn’t hear the ____ sound of footsteps outside her bedroom door.
questions.e: Fainter fits the comparison: the fainter sound of footsteps.

questions.q: Through his ____, the billionaire will be remembered for many centuries.
questions.e: Legacy is what a person leaves behind to be remembered by.

questions.q: Several individuals from ____ groups of society protested in front of the government offices today.
questions.e: Marginalized groups are pushed to the edge of society.

questions.q: Providing an excellent view of the landscape up to 120 miles in all directions, the mountain ____ over the surrounding countryside.
questions.e: To tower over means to rise high above.

questions.q: Some career choices are better suited for individuals with good problem-solving skills and ____ minds.
questions.e: Analytical minds examine problems carefully, which suits problem-solving.

questions.q: The government continues to disparage smoking because of its ____ effects on the body.
questions.e: Detrimental means harmful.

questions.q: The woman filed a lawsuit after her ex-husband continued to ____ her.
questions.e: Harass means to bother or trouble someone repeatedly.

sets.title: B. Closest in meaning (single words)
sets.intro: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word. 10 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Demented
questions.e: Demented means mad or insane; idiotic is closest.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Regress
questions.e: Regress means to go back to an earlier, worse state: backslide.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Slither
questions.e: Slither means to slide along the ground.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Heralded
questions.e: Heralded means announced with praise: praised.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Decamp
questions.e: Decamp means to leave suddenly: flee.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Coddle
questions.e: Coddle means to treat too gently, to pamper: satisfy is the nearest choice.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Barren
questions.e: Barren land produces nothing: unproductive.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Subjugate
questions.e: Subjugate means to bring under control by force: conquer.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Abstain
questions.e: Abstain means to hold back from doing something: refrain.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Pester
questions.e: Pester means to bother again and again: annoy.

sets.title: C. Synonyms in sentences
sets.intro: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to the word named in each question. In the bank the target words were not marked, so each is named here. 15 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to abides by: A good citizen abides by law.
questions.e: Abide by means to follow or obey: adheres to.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to abjure: We don’t force anyone to abjure his religion.
questions.e: Abjure means to give up or renounce solemnly.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to abounds in: His garden abounds in beautiful flowers.
questions.e: Abound in means to have plenty of: teems with.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to complexion: Your story puts a different complexion on the matter.
questions.e: Complexion here means the look or appearance of something.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to commotion: The city was in commotion during the electric blackout.
questions.e: Commotion means noisy confusion.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to commodious: They found their hotel room commodious.
questions.e: Commodious means roomy: spacious.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to clumsy: Harry is a clumsy boy constantly stumbling over his own feet.
questions.e: Clumsy means awkward in movement.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to chagrin: His refusal to go with us filled us with chagrin.
questions.e: Chagrin is annoyance or distress: vexation.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to authentic: The document bears an authentic signature.
questions.e: Authentic means real: genuine.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to bigoted: John is a bigoted young man.
questions.e: Bigoted means stubbornly intolerant: narrow-minded.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to bounteous: She is a woman of bounteous nature.
questions.e: Bounteous means giving freely: generous.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to brusque: Don’t be shocked if you are greeted with a brusque welcome.
questions.e: Brusque means abrupt and rude: curt.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to bypassed: The taxi driver bypassed the main street.
questions.e: Bypass means to go around: detoured.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to catastrophe: The flood was a catastrophe.
questions.e: Catastrophe means a sudden great disaster: calamity.

questions.q: Choose the word or phrase closest in meaning to cessation: The workers threatened a cessation of all activities if their demands were not met.
questions.e: Cessation means a stopping.

sets.title: D. Idioms and fixed expressions
sets.intro: Choose the word that completes each idiom or fixed expression. 10 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: By hook or by ____ he is determined to win the race.
questions.e: The idiom is by hook or by crook: by any means.

questions.q: Since you were at fault, you have to be brave enough to face the ____.
questions.e: To face the music means to accept the consequences.

questions.q: I can feel it in my ____ that something has gone wrong.
questions.e: To feel it in your bones means to be sure of something without proof.

questions.q: Tell me what you want to say directly. Don’t ____ about the bush.
questions.e: To beat about the bush means to avoid the main point.

questions.q: Only at the ____ hour did he inform us that he would not be coming for the interview.
questions.e: The eleventh hour means the last possible moment.

questions.q: I cannot make ____ of what the lecturer is saying.
questions.e: Cannot make head or tail of something means cannot understand it.

questions.q: The heartless man killed his brother in cold ____.
questions.e: In cold blood means cruelly and without emotion.

questions.q: The landlord told the tenant to move his things lock, stock and ____ out of the building.
questions.e: Lock, stock and barrel means everything, completely.

questions.q: The agreement between two companies was recorded in ____.
questions.e: In black and white means in writing.

questions.q: Zheming is upset that he always has to play second ____ to his brother.
questions.e: To play second fiddle means to have a less important role.

sets.title: E. Vocabulary multiple choice (2014)
sets.intro: Choose the word that best completes each sentence. 10 questions from the NIE exam bank. The original bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: You are ____ to be fined if you break the law.
questions.e: Liable means likely or legally responsible: liable to be fined.

questions.q: The accident occurred at the road ____.
questions.e: A junction is a place where roads meet.

questions.q: The king ordered his knights to ____ the rebellion.
questions.e: Suppress means to put down by force: suppress the rebellion.

questions.q: These are the few ____ available and you have to pick one of them.
questions.e: Options are the choices available.

questions.q: At the request of the defense lawyer, the judge ____ the trial.
questions.e: Adjourn means to postpone or pause a trial or meeting.

questions.q: The boy made a ____ of himself and was told off by the manager.
questions.e: Make a nuisance of yourself means to annoy others.

questions.q: You have to ____ by the rules of the club if you become members.
questions.e: Abide by the rules means to follow them.

questions.q: The prosecution ____ the evidence given by the expert witness to support its case.
questions.e: Cite means to quote as evidence: cited the evidence.

questions.q: He scolded them for failing to ____ with his instructions.
questions.e: Comply with means to obey instructions.

questions.q: One common ____ among successful businessmen is their strong determination to succeed.
questions.e: An aspect is one feature or part of something.

sets.title: F. Words from definitions
sets.intro: Choose the word that completes each definition. In the bank, the answer word was printed in brackets after each sentence, so here it is one of the four options. 18 questions from the NIE exam bank. The bank has no answer key, so the feedback was prepared by Claude: please check it against your own key.

questions.q: If something has never happened before, it is ____.
questions.e: Unprecedented means never having happened before.

questions.q: Water that is underground is in a(n) ____ location.
questions.e: Subterranean means underground (sub = under, terra = earth).

questions.q: I need to ____ in this situation. It is important to come in between these people and their fight.
questions.e: Intervene means to come between people to stop or change what is happening.

questions.q: A person who is very outgoing in dealing with others is a(n) ____.
questions.e: An extrovert is outgoing and sociable. An introvert is the opposite.

questions.q: If you carry goods out of one country, you ____ those goods.
questions.e: Export means to send goods out of a country. Import means to bring them in.

questions.q: To write or place a limit around something is to ____.
questions.e: Circumscribe means to draw a line around something or to limit it.

questions.q: To look at something again in order to make it better is to ____.
questions.e: Revise means to re-examine something and improve it.

questions.q: To send in something that you would like to place under consideration is to ____ it.
questions.e: Submit means to hand something in to be considered.

questions.q: To exchange information electronically from far away is to ____.
questions.e: Telecommunicate: tele (far) + communicate, to exchange information over a distance.

questions.q: A meeting where people get together to speak with each other is a(n) ____.
questions.e: A convocation is a formal gathering or assembly.

questions.q: If you come together again for a meeting, you ____ the meeting.
questions.e: Reconvene means to come together again (re = again, convene = meet).

questions.q: I am trying to ____ the place you are describing; I would like to see it in my mind.
questions.e: Visualize means to form a picture of something in your mind.

questions.q: Every time I express my opinion, you always ____ me; you always say the opposite of what I say.
questions.e: Contradict means to say the opposite of what someone says.

questions.q: The ____ in the card is really meaningful; I really like what is written inside it.
questions.e: An inscription is words written inside or on something.

questions.q: My friend is studying ____ because she thinks it is interesting to understand what people's handwriting means.
questions.e: Graphology is the study of handwriting.

questions.q: After the man's death a(n) ____ was conducted to determine how he had died.
questions.e: A post-mortem is an examination of a body after death to find the cause.

questions.q: These socks are ____; they are incorrectly paired.
questions.e: Mismatched means not matching or wrongly paired.

questions.q: Tom is quite a(n) ____ person; he is not at all outgoing.
questions.e: Introverted means shy and inward-looking, the opposite of outgoing.

sets.title: G. Word formation
sets.intro: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete each sentence. 25 questions from the NIE exam bank. Item 38 of the bank (working as a trainer or a trainee) was left out because both could be right. The bank has no answer key, so the answers and feedback were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: This insurance company is well-known for its ____. (to rely)
questions.e: Rely → reliability: the quality of being dependable.

questions.q: Those students are famous for their ____ to school and community. (to commit)
questions.e: Commit → commitment: dedication to a cause or place.

questions.q: He's very popular in school. He's really ____ and fun for his school. (to energize)
questions.e: Energize → energetic: an adjective, full of energy.

questions.q: I could hit myself. I made the same mistake twice in ____. (to succeed)
questions.e: The fixed phrase is twice in succession (one after the other).

questions.q: Meeting other people, for me, is a basic ____. (to need)
questions.e: The noun form of to need is need: a basic need.

questions.q: We are looking for a candidate with real ____ capacities. (to manage)
questions.e: An adjective is needed before capacities: managerial.

questions.q: Thanks for your ____ of my humble invitation. (to accept)
questions.e: Accept → acceptance: a noun after your ... of.

questions.q: The ____ time is at 9 o'clock. (to arrive)
questions.e: Arrive → arrival: a noun used before time (arrival time).

questions.q: You should ask for his ____ first. (to approve)
questions.e: Approve → approval: a noun after his.

questions.q: Could you send us 10 ____ brochures for distribution among our staff? (to add)
questions.e: Add → additional: an adjective meaning extra.

questions.q: ____ must be filed within five working days. (to complain)
questions.e: Complain → complaints: a plural noun is the subject of must be filed.

questions.q: They must have forgotten to add the ____ to this letter. (to enclose)
questions.e: Enclose → enclosure: a noun after the (the thing enclosed).

questions.q: It's tough being an ____ these days. (to apply)
questions.e: Apply → applicant: the person who applies.

questions.q: German cars are known for their ____. (to rely)
questions.e: Rely → reliability: the quality of being dependable.

questions.q: I usually have a sore throat after a night of ____ drinking and smoking. (to exceed)
questions.e: Exceed → excessive: an adjective meaning too much.

questions.q: We look forward to receiving your price ____. (to quote)
questions.e: Quote → quotation: a noun, a statement of the price.

questions.q: Payment will be effected on ____ of the goods. (to receive)
questions.e: The fixed phrase is on receipt of the goods.

questions.q: A five percent discount for regular customers is not really ____. (to accept)
questions.e: Accept → acceptable: an adjective after is not really.

questions.q: If your terms are ____, we may consider placing regular orders. (to satisfy)
questions.e: Satisfy → satisfactory: an adjective meaning good enough.

questions.q: Check if there is a ____ fee. (to cancel)
questions.e: Cancel → cancellation: a noun used before fee.

questions.q: Your ____ makes me disappointed. (to refuse)
questions.e: Refuse → refusal: a noun after Your.

questions.q: Let me introduce you to Helen, the management ____. (to assist)
questions.e: Assist → assistant: the person who assists.

questions.q: The successful candidate will be fully responsible for ____ profitable sales through the recruitment, direction, motivation and control of the direct sales force. (to maximize)
questions.e: After the preposition for, use the -ing form: maximizing.

questions.q: Your car looks dirty! You'd better take it to the car-washing place to have it ____. (to wash)
questions.e: Have something done uses the past participle: have it washed.

questions.q: You deserve appreciation and admiration for your ____ to our school. (to commit)
questions.e: Commit → commitment: a noun after your.

sets.title: H. Matching definitions to terms
sets.intro: Choose the term that matches each definition. In the bank, you matched 20 definitions to a list of 20 terms. Here each definition has four options taken from that list. 20 questions. The bank has no answer key, so the answers were prepared by Claude: please check them against your own key.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Logical or sensible.
questions.e: Rational: logical or sensible.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Being able to change places or replace something else.
questions.e: Interchangeable: being able to change places or replace something else.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Someone excessively devoted to or enthusiastic about a cause.
questions.e: Fanatic: someone excessively devoted to or enthusiastic about a cause.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? To make something real.
questions.e: Realization: to make something real.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? A dream.
questions.e: Vision: a dream.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? To explain in detail.
questions.e: Elaborate: to explain in detail.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Easily persuaded or swayed; submissive.
questions.e: Compliant: easily persuaded or swayed; submissive.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? To exhibit something a little too proudly.
questions.e: Flaunt: to exhibit something a little too proudly.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Feeling safe and certain.
questions.e: Security: feeling safe and certain.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? An overly vain person.
questions.e: Prima donna: an overly vain person.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? The full or complete range of things.
questions.e: Gamut: the full or complete range of things.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Accomplishing something rewarding.
questions.e: Achievement: accomplishing something rewarding.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? A lack of false pride; feeling modest.
questions.e: Humility: a lack of false pride; feeling modest.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Free from corruption or vice; honesty.
questions.e: Integrity: free from corruption or vice; honesty.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Wrongful treatment of a person or group due to bias or prejudice.
questions.e: Discrimination: wrongful treatment of a person or group due to bias or prejudice.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? A feeling arising when hindered in trying to reach a goal.
questions.e: Frustration: a feeling arising when hindered in trying to reach a goal.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Putting an assignment or task off until a later time; dawdling.
questions.e: Procrastination: putting an assignment or task off until a later time; dawdling.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? More of something than is necessary.
questions.e: Excess: more of something than is necessary.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Actions typified by a lack of planning or preparing.
questions.e: Impulsive: actions typified by a lack of planning or preparing.

questions.q: Which term matches this definition? Instinctive knowing; a feeling that something might happen.
questions.e: Intuition: instinctive knowing; a feeling that something might happen.
